subject: Re: Reactive Data Frame to Produce Plots

messages.subject: Re: Reactive Data Frame to Produce Plots
parts:
You need to create separate reactive expressions for each of the interesting values that need to change over time (gdp, gen_gov_balance_pc, etc.). And then call those reactive expressions to retrieve their values--you can't just invoke them and then refer to local variables that are inside them. I'd highly recommend viewing the Effective Reactive Programming videos from Shiny Developer Conference 2016:

https://www.rstudio.com/resources/webinars/shiny-developer-conference/
On Fri, Jun 9, 2017 at 8:18 AM Tom O'Keeffe <tomoke...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi,

My aim to is to give the user the ability to choose the country of which the data is visualised. But I am unsure how to do so without repeating the code. I've tried using the reactive({}) expression but it doesn't seem to work. Any advice would be greatly appreciated. 


#Data from my public dropbox. This is the non-financial transaction data from the Eurostat database.
#load(url("https://www.dropbox.com/s/td6s2zqc8m41qs0/NonFinData.RData?dl=1"))

server <- function(input, output, sessions) {
  
    #Want to give user ability to choose country
    DF <- reactive({
    tmp2 <-filter(NonFinData,geo.time==input$geo.time ,unit=="CP_MEUR")
    gdp<-filter(tmp2, na_item=="B1GQ", direct=="PAID")
    gdp_d <- subset(gdp, select = c("unit", "geo.time","time", "value"))
    gdp_d$value <- (gdp$value/lag(gdp$value,1) -1)*100
    

    #general govt balance
    gen_gov_balance<-filter(tmp2, na_item=="B9",direct=="PAID", sector=="S13")
    gen_gov_balance_pc<-subset(gen_gov_balance, select = c("unit", "geo.time","time", "value"))
    gen_gov_balance_pc$value<-as.numeric(as.character(gen_gov_balance_pc$value))
    gen_gov_balance_pc$value<-as.numeric(as.character(gen_gov_balance$value))/as.numeric(as.character(gdp$value))*100
    
    #Government expenditure
    gov_exp<-filter(tmp2, na_item=="OTE", direct=="PAID", sector=="S13")
    
    #government tax revenue
    gov_trev <- filter(tmp2, na_item == "OTR",sector == "S13", direct == "RECV")
    
    #theta - tax share
    theta <- subset(gov_trev, select = c("unit", "geo.time","time", "value"))
    theta$value<-as.numeric(as.character(gov_trev$value))/as.numeric(as.character(gdp$value))
    #Adjusted fiscal ratio
    AFR <- theta
    AFR$value<-as.numeric(as.character(gov_exp$value))/as.numeric(as.character(theta$value))
    
    })



  
output$plot<- renderPlotly({
  DF()
  if(input$figure==1){
    p1 <- plot_ly(gen_gov_balance_pc,x = gen_gov_balance_pc$time, y = gen_gov_balance_pc$value, type = "bar")%>%
      layout(title = "Figure 1 - General Government Balance", yaxis = list(title = "Percentage of GDP"), xaxis = list(title = "Time"))
    
  }else
    if(input$figure==2){
      p2<-plot_ly()%>%
        add_lines(x = gdp$time, y = gdp$value,line=list(width = 3), name = 'GDP') %>%
        add_lines(x = AFR$time, y = AFR$value, type = 'scatter', mode = 'lines',line=list(width = 3), name = 'AFR')%>%
        layout(title = "Figure 2 - Adjusted Fiscal Ratio and GDP",xaxis = list(title = 'Time'),yaxis = list(title = '€ in Millions'))
      
    }
})


Thanks for your help.
